newsitem.title: CHINA: China mulls rules on investment fund management.
newsitem.headline: China mulls rules on investment fund management.

text.p: China is close to approving draft regulations to govern the management of mutual investment funds and may permit the trial operation by up to four industrial investment funds, the official China Daily said on Tuesday.
Industrial investment funds were expected to become the third major finance channel for Chinese enterprises after bank loans and share issues, the newspaper said.

Two long-awaited draft regulations, on fund management and Sino-foreign cooperative fund management firms, were in the final stages of approval and were expected to clarify China's strategy on mutual fund development, it said.
If Beijing decided to push ahead with the development of industrial investment funds, it would first approve trial operations by one national fund and up to three regional ones, the newspaper added.
Foreign money would be barred from the pilot funds, which would be permitted to invest 20-30 percent of their assets in securities to ensure liquidity, it said but gave no details.
China has been working to clean up its market for mutual funds and last December lifted a three-year ban on new listings of stock investment funds.
Analysts say initial efforts to establish a successful investment fund system failed in the early 1990s because of inadequate supervision.
China had 75 mutual funds and 45 similar organisations, with total assets of around $8.0 billion, the China Daily said.
Most of the funds were small and had been operating irregularly because of insufficient knowledge and ineffective regulation, it said.

Excessive buying of shares in funds that repaid investments at the end of a fixed term had driven their market value higher than that of their assets, a situation that would cause trouble when repayment became due, it said but gave no details.
